This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Istanbul Airport in degrees Celsius on 2 Sep '26.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official forecasts from the National Weather Service and major meteorological services project a daily high near 91–92°F for Houston on September 2, 2026, under mostly cloudy skies with a 30–50% chance of afternoon showers and thunderstorms.** This aligns closely with the long-term average high of 91.5°F for the date and explains the heavy market weighting toward the 92–93°F bin (57.5% implied probability) and 94–95°F bin (39.5%).

Afternoon instability from Gulf moisture and daytime heating favors scattered storms that can limit peak temperatures through cloud cover and evaporative cooling, while light southwesterly winds and high dew points (near 75–78°F) support heat indices above 105°F without pushing actual air temperatures much higher. Recent observations through early afternoon have reached the low 90s, consistent with model consensus and reducing the odds of extremes above 96°F to just 6%.

The market’s tight clustering around the low-90s range reflects traders’ confidence in stable late-summer subtropical patterns rather than anomalous heat, with only modest probability assigned to slight forecast upward revisions.

eventMetadata.context_description: **An approaching early September Pacific storm system is suppressing daytime heating over Seattle on September 2, 2026, keeping the highest temperature in the mid-to-upper 60s.** Official National Weather Service and local forecasts indicate a high near 65–66°F under cloudy skies with showers likely, south winds of 10–20 mph, and periods of rain that limit solar insolation and promote evaporative cooling. These conditions align closely with the market’s leading 66–67°F (50%) and 68–69°F (30%) outcomes, which together capture the expected range under the current synoptic pattern. The setup deviates from the September 2 climatological average high of ~74°F, reflecting the storm’s influence on cloud cover, moisture, and boundary-layer mixing rather than clear-sky radiative heating. Updated model runs and surface observations through midday continue to support this cooler trajectory, with only modest upside risk if breaks in the clouds allow brief warming.

Resolution will depend on the official maximum recorded at the primary station.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Paris-Le Bourget Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=lfpb

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models and real-time observations position 30°C as the dominant outcome for Ankara’s September 3 high, with 31°C a clear secondary possibility.** Multiple authoritative sources, including PredictWind, Yr.no, and Turkish meteorological outlets, project an afternoon peak of 29–31°C under clear skies, light northeasterly flow, and negligible precipitation risk. Current surface conditions on September 2 show temperatures already reaching the upper 20s°C with dry air and high pressure dominating, supporting modest daytime heating into the low 30s°C without significant advection or cloud cover to suppress it.

Climatologically, early-September Ankara averages near 27°C, yet the present synoptic pattern—stable anticyclonic conditions and above-normal warmth—has kept recent highs at or above 30°C, aligning trader consensus with the 67% implied probability on 30°C and 25.5% on 31°C. Lower outcomes (29°C or below) receive only modest weight because models show little cooling influence before the daily maximum window. Higher thresholds (32°C+) remain improbable absent unexpected subsidence or southerly flow. With resolution imminent, the market aggregates the narrow uncertainty band typical of short-range deterministic forecasts for this location and season.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official forecasts from the Wuhan Meteorological Observatory highlight a primary driver of cooler conditions on September 3: residual influence from a tropical cyclone inverted trough, delivering scattered rain transitioning to cloudy skies with persistent northeasterly winds of 3–5 Beaufort and gusts to 6–7. These factors limit peak solar insolation and promote cold-air advection, supporting a consensus maximum near 27°C amid 50–95% humidity. Model spreads arise from variable rain timing and cloud persistence, which can suppress or allow brief warming episodes, while historical September climatology near 29°C provides context for the slight upward trader bias toward 28–29°C outcomes. New model runs and surface observations tomorrow morning will refine resolution thresholds.

Official observations from the primary Manila station will determine resolution once the full diurnal cycle completes.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent synoptic patterns and forecast consensus position 18–20°C as the most probable maximum temperature range for Buenos Aires on September 3.** 

An incoming cold front and associated moisture from the southwest are expected to increase cloud cover and bring showers or thunderstorms, limiting daytime heating after today’s warmer readings near 21–23°C. Multiple numerical weather models and official guidance (including Servicio Meteorológico Nacional trends) converge on a daytime high of 17–19°C under mostly cloudy skies and moderate westerly winds, consistent with early-spring climatology where September average highs sit near 19–20°C. 

The market’s heavy weighting toward 19°C (56%) and 20°C (28%) reflects this consensus, tempered by typical forecast uncertainty in frontal timing and exact cloud/rain coverage that could allow brief clearing and slightly higher readings or suppress temperatures further. Updated model runs and official briefings tomorrow morning will provide the final data ahead of market resolution.

title: Highest temperature in Tel Aviv on September 4?

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent forecasts from multiple meteorological sources indicate peak daytime temperatures in Tel Aviv on September 4, 2026, will likely reach 31–32°C under stable high-pressure conditions, clear skies, and light westerly winds.** This aligns closely with the market’s heavy weighting toward 32°C (70.5% implied probability), followed by 33°C (15.0%), reflecting trader consensus on a modest warming above the historical early-September average high of roughly 29–30°C.

Key scientific drivers include persistent subsidence from a regional high-pressure ridge promoting strong daytime insolation with minimal cloud cover, combined with moderate humidity and sea-breeze moderation from the Mediterranean that typically caps extremes. Model outputs (including GFS-derived guidance) show consistent afternoon maxima near 31–32°C, with limited spread across runs and no incoming fronts or significant moisture to alter the thermal profile. Historical analogs for early September under similar synoptic patterns rarely exceed 33–34°C without anomalous heat advection.

No major forecast revisions or extreme-heat advisories have emerged in the past 48 hours, supporting the tight clustering around 32°C as the most probable resolution outcome while leaving modest room for a 33°C spike if boundary-layer mixing or slight model bias favors warmer verification. Updated model runs and official Israel Meteorological Service briefings over the next 24–48 hours will provide the final data points before market resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from the Hong Kong Observatory and numerical models indicate a highest temperature on September 4 most likely in the 25–29°C range, with 28–29°C favored amid persistent cloud cover and scattered showers tied to Tropical Cyclone Sa Del. Northwesterly winds of 4–5 on the Beaufort scale, elevated humidity above 70%, and reduced insolation from widespread cloud suppress peak daytime heating compared with clearer climatological norms for early September. Model consensus shows limited warming potential unless the system weakens faster than expected, while any clearing could briefly allow readings near 30°C. Traders assign roughly equal weight to 28°C and 29°C outcomes, reflecting genuine short-term forecast uncertainty ahead of the next HKO update.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecast models from sources including the China Meteorological Administration and international ensembles point to persistent cloud cover, moderate northeast winds, and scattered showers as the main factors capping Shanghai’s daytime maximum near 30–31 °C on September 4. These conditions are expected to limit solar heating while keeping humidity elevated, consistent with early-September climatology for the region. Model consensus across multiple runs shows little support for extremes above 32 °C or below 29 °C, aligning with the market’s heavy weighting toward the 30 °C and 31 °C outcomes. Updated guidance from official agencies over the next 48 hours will be the key driver of any final shifts in implied probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Dry southwest monsoon conditions, confirmed in the Meteorological Service Singapore advisory issued September 1, are the main driver behind the 66.5% market-implied probability for a 33°C high on September 4.** 

Prevailing southeasterly to southwesterly winds, below-average rainfall, and mostly fair skies with limited afternoon cloud cover are expected to allow strong daytime heating, consistent with the official outlook of 33–35°C maxima on most days in the first fortnight. Short-range model guidance and hourly forecasts show afternoon peaks near 33°C under these conditions, with only low chances of localized thundery showers that could briefly suppress temperatures. Historical September averages near 31–32°C provide context, but the current dry spell favors the upper end of the normal range. Traders appear to weigh the balance between this consensus forecast and residual uncertainty from possible haze or isolated convection, keeping 32°C as the secondary outcome at 26.5%. Updated official guidance closer to the date will be the key catalyst for any shifts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent numerical weather prediction runs from major models show Mexico City maximum temperatures on September 4 most likely reaching 26–27 °C under partly cloudy skies with scattered afternoon convection. This consensus drives the near-even market-implied odds between those two outcomes. Typical early-September climatology features average highs near 24–25 °C at the city’s 2,240 m elevation, but weak steering flow and moderate moisture support localized heating that can push peaks 1–2 °C higher before showers develop. Key variables separating 26 °C from 27 °C include the precise timing and coverage of cloud build-up, boundary-layer mixing depth, and urban heat-island amplification. Updated model guidance and satellite observations over the next 48 hours will refine these details ahead of market resolution.
